artist.name: Leanna Firestone
artist.short_description: Leanna Firestone: an Afterglow editorial discovery candidate in indie pop.
artist.biography: Leanna Firestone is an American indie-pop singer-songwriter whose writing is frequently personal, conversational, and self-aware. Her artist biography describes how posting music on social media helped her build an audience before the release of early tracks including “Strawberry Mentos” and “Least Favorite Only Child.” Her catalogue subsequently expanded to “Smitten,” “Diet Coke,” and “You Just Didn’t Like Me That Much,” as well as the later album The Answer. In a firsthand interview with The New Nine, Firestone explained that the idea for “You Just Didn’t Like Me That Much” was prompted by reading an online observation that reframed a painful relationship experience. This interview is a useful source for Afterglow because it explicitly addresses the song’s meaning rather than merely discussing the artist’s wider career. Her songs provide a compelling recommendation path from Sara Kays and Sadie Jean toward writing that is more humorous or sharply phrased without losing its emotional focus. All connections to other artists are Afterglow editorial suggestions, not collaborations or endorsements unless independently documented.
